meaning:
βλάσφημος, -ον
(βλασ-, of uncertain deriv., see Thayer, Boisacq; + φήμη, speech), [in LXX: Isa.66:3 (מְבָרֵךְ אָוֶן), Wis.1:6, Sir.3:16, 2Ma.9:28 10:4, 36 * ;]
(a) evil-speaking, slanderous, blasphemous: Act.6:11, 2Ti.3:2, 2Pe.2:11 (cf. Ju 9);
(b) as subst. a blasphemer: 1Ti.1:13 (Cremer, 570).
† (AS)

elsewhere.note: Then they secretly induced men to say, “We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and God.”
although I used to be a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent. However, I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
For men will be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy,
whereas angels, though greater in might and power, don’t bring a railing judgment against them before the Lord.
